mission.title: Install and Configure Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (OCP)
mission.description: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) is a comprehensive Kubernetes distribution that provides an enterprise-grade platform for deploying and managing containerized applications. It includes developer and operational tools for building, deploying, and managing applications in a hybrid cloud environment. Key trade-offs include the complexity of installation and management versus the rich feature set and support provided.

steps.title: Install the OpenShift CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the OpenShift command-line interface (CLI) which is essential for interacting with the OpenShift cluster.

```bash

curl -LO https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/latest/openshift-client-linux-4.17.0.tar.gz

tar -xvf openshift-client-linux-4.17.0.tar.gz

sudo mv oc kubectl /usr/local/bin/

```

> Download the OpenShift CLI for version 4.17.0.
> Extract the downloaded tarball.
> Move the binaries to a directory in your PATH.

steps.title: Create an OpenShift cluster
steps.description:
This step creates a new OpenShift cluster with the specified version and node count.

```bash

openshift-install create cluster --dir=mycluster --log-level=info

```

> Replace 'mycluster' with your desired cluster directory.

steps.title: Set up kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step configures your kubeconfig file to access the OpenShift cluster.

```bash

export KUBECONFIG=`pwd`/mycluster/auth/kubeconfig

```

> Set the KUBECONFIG environment variable to the cluster's kubeconfig.

steps.title: Verify cluster nodes
steps.description:
This step checks the status of the nodes in the OpenShift cluster to ensure they are ready.

```bash

oc get nodes

```

> List all nodes and their status.

steps.title: Post-install configuration
steps.description:
This step sets up additional features such as monitoring and autoscaling.

```bash

oc apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openshift/cluster-monitoring-operator/master/deploy/cluster-monitoring-operator.yaml

oc apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openshift/cluster-autoscaler/master/deploy/cluster-autoscaler-operator.yaml

```

> Deploy the cluster monitoring operator.
> Deploy the cluster autoscaler operator.

uninstall.title: Remove the OpenShift cluster
uninstall.description:
This step will delete the OpenShift cluster and all associated resources, which may result in data loss.

```bash

openshift-install destroy cluster --dir=mycluster --log-level=info

```

> Ensure you have backups of any important data before proceeding.

uninstall.title: Clean up orphaned resources
uninstall.description:
This step removes any orphaned resources that may remain after cluster deletion.

```bash

aws ec2 describe-instances --filters 'Name=tag:Name,Values=mycluster*' --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].InstanceId' --output text | xargs aws ec2 terminate-instances

```

> Replace 'mycluster' with your cluster name.
commands: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters 'Name=tag:Name,Values=mycluster*' --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].InstanceId' --output text | xargs aws ec2 terminate-instances

upgrade.title: Upgrade OpenShift cluster
upgrade.description:
This step includes backing up the current state, upgrading the cluster, and verifying the upgrade.

```bash

oc adm upgrade --to-image=registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose:4.17.0

oc get clusterversion

```

> Upgrade to OpenShift version 4.17.0.
> Verify the cluster version after the upgrade.

troubleshooting.title: Error: Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The kubeconfig file may not be pointing to the correct cluster or the cluster's certificate is not trusted.

**Fix:**
Ensure the KUBECONFIG environment variable is set correctly and the cluster's CA certificate is included.

troubleshooting.title: Error: no nodes available in cluster
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** All nodes may be in a NotReady state due to insufficient resources or misconfiguration.

**Fix:**
Check the node status with 'oc get nodes' and troubleshoot based on the output.

troubleshooting.title: Error: ImagePullBackOff
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The specified image may not exist or the image pull secret may be missing.

**Fix:**
Verify the image name and ensure the image pull secret is correctly configured.

troubleshooting.title: Error: Failed to create pod sandbox
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur due to insufficient resources on the node or network issues.

**Fix:**
Check node resource availability and network configurations.

versionNotes.changes: Introduced support for new container storage interface (CSI) drivers, enhanced security features, and improved monitoring capabilities.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated legacy networking plugins in favor of CNI-based solutions.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: If upgrading from version 4.16, ensure to migrate any legacy networking configurations to the new CNI-based solutions.

resolution.summary: You should see a list of nodes with 'Ready' status when running 'oc get nodes'.
